name: Jezero crater
sources: MOLA-HRSC blended DEM 200 m v2 (Fergason, Hare & Laura 2018, USGS Astrogeology)

albedo: TES Lambert (bolometric) albedo, global map Mars_MGS_TES_Albedo_mosaic_global_7410m.tif (7.4 km/px), mean over the 30 km footprint (Christensen et al. 2001, JGR 106(E10):23823, doi:10.1029/2000JE001370; USGS Astrogeology mosaic). One definition for every Mars target; a 10 km footprint holds only a few TES pixels

ti_class: THEMIS-derived thermal inertia of Jezero crater (Edwards & Buz 2021, Zenodo, doi:10.5281/zenodo.4931348), median 226 SI over the 30 km footprint (100% covered) -> class 1 with the Mars bins 100/250/600/1200

tmin_k / tmax_k: MEDA ground temperature (TIRS) along Perseverance's traverse, Ls 13-203: daily max 273 / 277 / 293 K and min 192 / 191 / 189 K at Ls 25 / 90 / 180 (Munguira et al. 2023, JGR Planets 128, e2022JE007559, doi:10.1029/2022JE007559) -> warmest 293 K, coldest 189 K. Northern winter is not covered, so the coldest-month minimum is probably a little lower

litho_class: crater floor is igneous - Seitah olivine cumulate, Maaz lava flows (Farley et al. 2022, Science, doi:10.1126/science.abo2196); the delta in the west of the window is sedimentary (class 3) - Sofia to confirm
ice_idx: 18N is far equatorward of the near-surface ice stability zone (~50 deg; Morgan et al. 2021, Nature Astronomy, doi:10.1038/s41550-020-01290-z)
lowsun_frac: analytic sun geometry, obliquity 25.19 deg (engine/illumination.py) - exact for latitude, ignores local horizon
blurb: Ancient lake delta; Perseverance landing site.

name: Gale crater
sources: MOLA-HRSC blended DEM 200 m v2 (Fergason, Hare & Laura 2018, USGS Astrogeology)

albedo: TES Lambert (bolometric) albedo, global map Mars_MGS_TES_Albedo_mosaic_global_7410m.tif (7.4 km/px), mean over the 30 km footprint (Christensen et al. 2001, JGR 106(E10):23823, doi:10.1029/2000JE001370; USGS Astrogeology mosaic). One definition for every Mars target; a 10 km footprint holds only a few TES pixels
ti_class: THEMIS TI 250-410 over most of the landing region, layered units 400-500 (Fergason et al. 2012, Space Sci Rev, doi:10.1007/s11214-012-9891-3) -> class 2

tmin_k / tmax_k: REMS ground temperature, daily max ~250-290 K and daily min ~170-210 K over the year (Gomez-Elvira et al., Granada 2017 workshop) - measured on the crater floor; Mount Sharp is a bit colder
litho_class: Aeolis Mons (Mount Sharp) is a thick stack of sedimentary rocks (Curiosity results) -> class 3
ice_idx: 5S is far equatorward of the near-surface ice stability zone (Morgan et al. 2021)
lowsun_frac: analytic sun geometry, obliquity 25.19 deg (engine/illumination.py) - exact for latitude, ignores local horizon
blurb: Layered sediments and sulfates; Curiosity landing site.

name: Taurus-Littrow valley (Apollo 17)
sources: LOLA + Kaguya TC merged DEM, SLDEM2015 512 ppd (Barker et al. 2016, USGS Astrogeology)

albedo: LOLA normal albedo at 1064 nm, GDR map LDAM_10_FLOAT.LBL, mean over the 30 km footprint (Lucey et al. 2014, JGR Planets 119:1665, doi:10.1002/2013JE004592). LOLA lights the ground with its own laser at zero phase, so one definition works in polar shadow and at Apollo 17. Not the Earth column's quantity (MODIS broadband shortwave albedo): one wavelength at zero phase reads higher than a broadband albedo of the same ground
ti_class: regolith-covered valley floor (old mare regolith ~14 m thick; Lucchitta 1992, LPI Workshop on Geology of the Apollo 17 Landing Site) -> class 1
tmin_k / tmax_k: Diviner, ~387-397 K at noon and ~95 K before sunrise near the equator (Williams et al. 2017, Icarus, doi:10.1016/j.icarus.2016.08.012); 20N noon is a few K lower

litho_class: basalt-flooded valley floor under a dark pyroclastic mantle (Muehlberger et al. 1973, Science, doi:10.1126/science.182.4113.672) -> class 1; the massifs in the window are feldspathic breccia (class 2) - check the majority class with the USGS map
ice_idx: no permanently shadowed regions at 20N (lunar PSRs are polar)
lowsun_frac: analytic sun geometry, obliquity 1.54 deg (engine/illumination.py) - exact for latitude, ignores local horizon
blurb: Apollo 17 landing site: ground truth for the method.

name: Jezero western delta front
sources: MOLA-HRSC blended DEM 200 m v2 (Fergason, Hare & Laura 2018, USGS Astrogeology)
centre: western fan unit NHjf2 (18.48N 77.39E) in Sun & Stack 2020, USGS SIM 3464, doi:10.3133/sim3464

albedo: TES Lambert (bolometric) albedo, global map Mars_MGS_TES_Albedo_mosaic_global_7410m.tif (7.4 km/px), mean over the 10 km footprint (Christensen et al. 2001, JGR 106(E10):23823, doi:10.1029/2000JE001370; USGS Astrogeology mosaic). One definition for every Mars target; a 10 km footprint holds only a few TES pixels

ti_class: THEMIS-derived thermal inertia of Jezero crater (Edwards & Buz 2021, Zenodo, doi:10.5281/zenodo.4931348), median 229 SI over the 10 km footprint (100% covered) -> class 1 with the Mars bins 100/250/600/1200

tmin_k / tmax_k: MEDA ground temperature (TIRS) along Perseverance's traverse, Ls 13-203: daily max 273 / 277 / 293 K and min 192 / 191 / 189 K at Ls 25 / 90 / 180 (Munguira et al. 2023, JGR Planets 128, e2022JE007559, doi:10.1029/2022JE007559) -> warmest 293 K, coldest 189 K. Northern winter is not covered, so the coldest-month minimum is probably a little lower - extrapolated to the delta front, a few km from the crater-floor traverse
litho_class: deltaic sedimentary rocks of the western fan front, deposited in a lake (Perseverance Delta Front campaign; Sun & Stack 2020, USGS SIM 3464, unit NHjf2) -> class 3
ice_idx: 18N is far equatorward of the near-surface ice stability zone (Morgan et al. 2021)
lowsun_frac: analytic sun geometry, obliquity 25.19 deg (engine/illumination.py) - exact for latitude, ignores local horizon
blurb: Lake delta front in Jezero crater; the sedimentary target for the astrobiology profile.

name: Shackleton crater and rim
sources: LOLA south polar DEM LDEM_80S_40MPP_ADJ (Barker et al. 2023, PSJ 4:183, doi:10.3847/PSJ/acf3e1; data doi:10.60903/gsfcpgda-lola-spole)
centre: IAU Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature, Shackleton (feature 5450), diameter 20.9 km - the 15 km circle covers the whole crater and rim

ice_idx: share of the 30 km footprint in permanent shadow, PGDA PSR map LPSR_75S_120M_201608.JP2 (Mazarico et al. 2011, Icarus 211:1066, doi:10.1016/j.icarus.2010.10.030). It is the AREA of cold traps, not a measured amount of ice: landing regions are picked on sunlit ridges, so the share is small by design. Shadow is modelled from LOLA topography; LEND hydrogen not folded in yet

litho_class: south-polar terrain is feldspathic highland (crater, basin and massif material, no mare) on the Unified Geologic Map of the Moon (Fortezzo et al. 2020) -> class 2; regional call, per-target unit check still to do

ti_class: class 1 (fine regolith, as at Apollo 17), extrapolated, not measured here - no Diviner thermophysical map reaches the poles: the H-parameter map covers 70S-70N (Hayne et al. 2017, JGR Planets 122:2371, doi:10.1002/2017JE005387) and so do the rock-abundance mosaics (Powell et al. 2023, JGR Planets 128, doi:10.1029/2022JE007532). Hayne et al. find the regolith fines globally uniform, which is what the extrapolation rests on

context.psr_share_50km (shown, not scored): share of the 50 km circle around the centre in permanent shadow, same model, PGDA PSR map LPSR_75S_120M_201608.JP2 - the cold traps within reach of a base here

tmin_k / tmax_k / diurnal_amp_k: Diviner bolometric surface temperature, Global Cumulative Product 90S-80S (all nadir data Jul 2009 - Apr 2015 in 0.5 x 0.5 deg bins x 15 min local time; Williams et al. 2017, Icarus 283:300, doi:10.1016/j.icarus.2016.08.012; PDS bundle doi:10.17189/wj0s-w188). Per bin the coldest and warmest local time of the mean day, then the mean over the 30 km footprint. Seasons are averaged together, so against the warmest-/coldest-month definition tmax_k reads low and tmin_k high (the seasonal 240 m polar maps, Williams et al. 2019, JGR Planets 124:2505, would fix it but are ~30 GB)

context.tmin_coldest_k (shown, not scored): the coldest 0.5 deg bin in the footprint, same Diviner product; at full resolution the permanently shadowed floors are colder still (Paige et al. 2010, Science 330:479, doi:10.1126/science.1187726)

albedo: LOLA normal albedo at 1064 nm, GDR map LDAM_50S_1000M_FLOAT.LBL, mean over the 30 km footprint (Lucey et al. 2014, JGR Planets 119:1665, doi:10.1002/2013JE004592). LOLA lights the ground with its own laser at zero phase, so one definition works in polar shadow and at Apollo 17. Not the Earth column's quantity (MODIS broadband shortwave albedo): one wavelength at zero phase reads higher than a broadband albedo of the same ground
lowsun_frac: analytic sun geometry, obliquity 1.54 deg (engine/illumination.py) - exact for latitude, ignores local horizon
blurb: Crater at the lunar south pole: near-permanently lit rim around a permanently shadowed floor.

litho_class: south-polar terrain is feldspathic highland (crater, basin and massif material, no mare) on the Unified Geologic Map of the Moon (Fortezzo et al. 2020) -> class 2; regional call, per-target unit check still to do

ti_class: class 1 (fine regolith, as at Apollo 17), extrapolated, not measured here - no Diviner thermophysical map reaches the poles: the H-parameter map covers 70S-70N (Hayne et al. 2017, JGR Planets 122:2371, doi:10.1002/2017JE005387) and so do the rock-abundance mosaics (Powell et al. 2023, JGR Planets 128, doi:10.1029/2022JE007532). Hayne et al. find the regolith fines globally uniform, which is what the extrapolation rests on

context.psr_share_50km (shown, not scored): share of the 50 km circle around the centre in permanent shadow, same model, PGDA PSR map LPSR_75S_120M_201608.JP2 - the cold traps within reach of a base here

tmin_k / tmax_k / diurnal_amp_k: Diviner bolometric surface temperature, Global Cumulative Product 90S-80S (all nadir data Jul 2009 - Apr 2015 in 0.5 x 0.5 deg bins x 15 min local time; Williams et al. 2017, Icarus 283:300, doi:10.1016/j.icarus.2016.08.012; PDS bundle doi:10.17189/wj0s-w188). Per bin the coldest and warmest local time of the mean day, then the mean over the 30 km footprint. Seasons are averaged together, so against the warmest-/coldest-month definition tmax_k reads low and tmin_k high (the seasonal 240 m polar maps, Williams et al. 2019, JGR Planets 124:2505, would fix it but are ~30 GB)

context.tmin_coldest_k (shown, not scored): the coldest 0.5 deg bin in the footprint, same Diviner product; at full resolution the permanently shadowed floors are colder still (Paige et al. 2010, Science 330:479, doi:10.1126/science.1187726)

albedo: LOLA normal albedo at 1064 nm, GDR map LDAM_50S_1000M_FLOAT.LBL, mean over the 30 km footprint (Lucey et al. 2014, JGR Planets 119:1665, doi:10.1002/2013JE004592). LOLA lights the ground with its own laser at zero phase, so one definition works in polar shadow and at Apollo 17. Not the Earth column's quantity (MODIS broadband shortwave albedo): one wavelength at zero phase reads higher than a broadband albedo of the same ground
lowsun_frac: analytic sun geometry, obliquity 1.54 deg (engine/illumination.py) - exact for latitude, ignores local horizon
blurb: Nobile Rim 1, one of NASA's nine candidate crew landing regions near the lunar south pole (announced for Artemis III, Oct 2024).
